title: Heavy bleeding — press hard and do not let go
applies_to: Someone bleeding fast, soaking through cloth, or bleeding that will not slow down.

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid
Committee on Tactical Combat Casualty Care, Tourniquet application guidance
citations.section: Limb tourniquet placement and time recording

steps.text: Call for help now. If someone else is there, tell them to call while you start.
Press hard on the wound with a clean cloth. If you have no cloth, press with your bare hand.
Keep pressing without letting go. Do not lift the cloth to look at the wound.
If blood soaks through, put another cloth on top and press harder. Leave the first cloth where it is.
If the wound is on an arm or a leg, lift that arm or leg higher than the chest while you keep pressing.
After a few minutes of hard pressing, check whether the bleeding has slowed. If it has, keep pressing and wait for help.
If it is an arm or a leg and the bleeding will not stop, tie a wide band, called a tourniquet, about 5 cm above the wound. Twist or pull it tight until the bleeding stops.
Look at a clock and remember the time you tightened the band. Say that time out loud to the ambulance crew when they arrive.
Keep the person lying down. Cover them with a coat or blanket so they stay warm.

do_not: Do not pull out glass, metal, or anything else stuck in the wound. Press around it instead and leave it in place.
Do not loosen or take off the tight band once the bleeding has stopped. Only the hospital should remove it.
Do not use string, wire, or a shoelace as the band. A thin band cuts into the skin and does not stop the bleeding.
Do not give them anything to eat or drink.
Do not put a tight band around the neck, chest, or belly. Press hard on those wounds instead.
escalate_if: They go pale, cold, sweaty, or confused — they are losing too much blood. Say this on the phone when you call.
They stop answering you and stop breathing normally — start pushing on the chest.
Blood is spurting out in time with the heartbeat — go straight to the tight band if it is an arm or a leg.
